title: Variant ghosting caused region-staggered fanout and capacity spike - remediation & follow-ups
creator: Anika Rao
description: Summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~02:41 UTC we observed a sudden cross-region traffic fanout that exhausted Dedicated pools in APAC and caused elevated error rates and timeouts for a subset of customers. The root trigger was a combination of a canary variant marked with an incorrect 'sticky=true' tag and a policy snapshot TTL mismatch between controllers, which produced transient 'ghost' variant entries in the policy mesh. Those ghost entries caused requests to be routed sequentially (region-staggered fanout) instead of short-circuiting, multiplying backend load. This ticket records the investigation thread, short-term mitigations, and longer-term action items.
timeline: 2026-03-10 02:41 UTC - Alert: Dedicated APAC pool error rate rises to 12% (SLO breach threshold 1%).
2026-03-10 02:44 UTC - On-call routed to routing team; initial theory: autoscaler regression or capacity leak.
2026-03-10 02:50 UTC - Router traces show same request ID hitting multiple region proxies sequentially with different variant IDs.
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Dispatched emergency policy snapshot refresh to controllers; partial reduction in fanout observed.
2026-03-10 03:18 UTC - Identified a recent canary rollout (PMX-19) that accidentally set 'sticky=true' on variant tag; this surfaced in snapshot diff.
2026-03-10 03:32 UTC - Hotfix deployed: rollback the canary tag and force-coalesce policy snapshots for 3 minutes; error rates returned near baseline by 03:47 UTC.
2026-03-10 04:10 UTC - Post-incident telemetry capture completed and runbook initiated for full RCA.
2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - Deep dive completed: policy TTL desynchronization root cause confirmed; details in root_cause field.
2026-03-12 14:00 UTC - Draft of action items and proposed safeguards circulated to platform and runtime leads.
root_cause: Two independent regressions combined: (1) A canary rollout pipeline change (PMX-19) introduced an opt-in tag 'sticky=true' for model variants but the rollout job applied the tag to the canary variant without validating compatibility with routing policies. The tag caused variant affinity metadata to be written, which is normally cleaned up during snapshot reconciliation. (2) A recent change to snapshot propagation reduced the default policy TTL from 45s to 5s for high-frequency routes (ENG-421314). Under load this created windowed inconsistencies: controllers sometimes replayed stale variant entries that were not fully garbage-collected, leading to transient 'ghost' variant entries in the distributed policy mesh. The router's fallback logic attempted sequential region failover on what looked like distinct variants, yielding region-staggered fanout and multiplier effect on capacity consumption.
mitigations: Immediate: Rolled back the canary tag and forced full snapshot reconciliation across controllers (completed 03:32 UTC).
Short-term: Temporarily increased policy snapshot TTL to 60s for affected clusters while we deploy fixes (applied 03:40 UTC).
Medium-term: Added router-side dedup check for variant fingerprint within 2s window to prevent sequential re-routing for same logical request.
Monitoring: Added dedicated dashboard panels for per-request multi-region traces and variant-fingerprint churn, plus alert thresholds for >2 regional handoffs per request.
Communication: Notified customers impacted (via SEs) and updated status page; customers with Dedicated pools received post-incident notes and recommended config tweaks.
action_items: AI-1 (owner: Marco Valdez) - Harden canary rollout pipeline to validate route-compatibility tags before applying; add gating checks that detect 'sticky' vs policy semantics. due: 2026-03-20

AI-2 (owner: Priya Sengupta) - Revert the low TTL change for snapshot propagation and implement a test harness that simulates snapshot convergence under high QPS. dependent: ENG-421314. due: 2026-03-18
AI-3 (owner: Samuel Ortiz) - Implement router deduplication for variant fingerprints (2s sliding window) and add unit + integration tests. due: 2026-03-25
AI-4 (owner: Elena Park) - Publish an incident-runbook entry for 'ghost variant' detection with runbook playbook steps and CLI commands to force snapshot coalesce. due: 2026-03-17
AI-5 (owner: Security) - Confirm tagging metadata does not leak PII or credentials in policy snapshots; file audit if any sensitive metadata found. due: 2026-03-22
AI-6 (owner: Observability team) - Create dashboard and alert: "multi-region-handoff-rate" and run a 72h retrospective alert to surface recurrence. due: 2026-03-16
AI-7 (owner: PM - Lila Nguyen) - Update rollout playbook to require canary compatibility sign-off from Routing platform for variant-affinity changes. due: 2026-03-19

resolution: Hotfix rollback + snapshot coalesce returned systems to normal and prevented further capacity burn. Root cause is a combination of rollout tag misuse and a snapshot TTL regression. Multiple action items assigned to prevent recurrence and strengthen tests/observability.
next_steps: Track completion of AI-1..AI-7 and confirm no recurrence in 30 days.
Run a post-deployment chaos test that simulates controller restart + canary tag changes to validate snapshot convergence.
Update SLAs/incident FAQ to include guidance for customers on Dedicated pool configuration if non-default routing tags are used.
